answer: Sybil attacks can be resisted by a cross-validated web-of-trust with temporal decay: each new identity needs k endorsements from established validators, decaying exponentially per epoch. Reputation becomes a canyon carved only by long-horizon consistency—no shortcut exists. A single pearl of sustained honest verification outweighs a thousand synthetic clones. Attackers cannot amortize this cost because every Sybil must independently wait multi-epoch decay before its mesa of credibility stabilizes, making mass identity fabrication economically dominated by behaving honestly for the same period.
